The 9-point
action plan for financial freedom

blocks.caption:
Nine money habits, from saving first to
checking your old investments.

blocks.html:
# Habit Details from the lecture
1 Save before you spend Save first, then spend the rest. Save at least 20%. Sports people and actors earn for only 10–15 years, so they should save much more (even 95%). Example: ₹100 a day × 20 days = ₹2,000.
2 Keep an emergency fund 3–6 months of expenses, in a fixed deposit or liquid mutual fund.
3 Buy term insurance Cover = about 100 × monthly income. Salary ₹25,000 → cover ₹25 lakh, costing about ₹3,500 a year (₹10 a day) at age 24–25. No endowment or whole-life policies when young.
4 Buy your own health insurance Don’t rely only on your company’s policy; you may change jobs. It costs about ₹4,000 a year when young. One hospital bill can be ₹2–10 lakh.
5 Diversify your assets Don’t put all your eggs in one basket. Put at most 20% (30% if very sure) of your net worth in your own business. Net worth ₹10 lakh → at most ₹2–3 lakh in the business. Keep 5–10% in cash for opportunities.
6 Start investing for retirement early You’ll have about 30 years of outflows with no salary.
7 Do SIPs for future goals SIP = Systematic Investment Plan: invest a fixed amount every month (₹100, ₹500, or more) in mutual funds.
8 Plan taxes in April, not March Plan at the start of the year. Example: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) under Section 80C, about ₹12,500 a month = ₹1.5 lakh a year.
9 Make sense of existing investments Check nominations, bank details and addresses (see below). Write a will if you own assets.

What to do with your
existing investments

blocks.html:
• Nominations: before marriage, usually parents; after marriage, often your spouse.
  • Bank details: if you move abroad, convert your account to an NRO account.
  • Addresses: update them everywhere (including Aadhaar) when you move.
  • Link each investment to a goal: “This one is for retirement.”
  • Keep all documents together. The lecture says about ₹16,000 crore lies unclaimed with banks and about ₹18,000 crore with LIC, because families didn’t know about the accounts or the details were wrong.
  • Share passwords and logins safely with family, so they can access things if something happens to you.
  • Know your CAGR (yearly growth rate). See the Returns page.

Six

blocks.html:
1. Know yourself: your curve, your stage, how you earn.
  2. Investment options: a long time horizon means you can take more risk, because higher risk can bring higher reward.
  3. Diversification: don’t put everything in one basket, including your own business.
  4. Risk vs reward:

  5. Timing: perfect timing is impossible. But if markets fall a lot (like during COVID) and your horizon is 10–15 years, it can be a good time to invest. A one-year recession matters less over 15–20 years.
  6. Role of your advisor: what does your advisor gain from what they sell you? Avoid herd mentality.

blocks.html:
Lecture example — Mr. Vijay’s flat Mr. Vijay bought a 15-year-old 2BHK in Chennai for ₹1 crore in December 2017. He sold it for ₹1.5 crore in December 2022 (5 years). He paid ₹2 lakh brokerage. (Tax is ignored here.)

  • Gain = ₹50 lakh − ₹2 lakh = ₹48 lakh → simple ROI = 48%.
  • “Per year” the simple way: 48 ÷ 5 = 9.6%. Most people stop here.
  • CAGR: (148 ÷ 100)^(1/5) − 1 = 8.16% a year.

The real yearly return is 8.16%, not 9.6%. That is 1.44 points less, or about 15% lower. And 8% is barely above food inflation of 7%.

sections.title: Employee vs Entrepreneur — Taking Calculated Risks

blocks.html: Start here Out of 100 new companies, only about 15 are still alive after 3 years. Yet some of those 15 change the world. Should you take a job or start a business? There is no single right answer. But there is a smart way to decide.

High risk, high reward

blocks.html:
• Entrepreneurship = high risk, high reward.

  • Why do the rest fail? Cash-flow problems, no customers, changing technology, or wrong assumptions.
  • A middle path: join a startup as an employee, but think like an entrepreneur. You get some of the rewards with less risk.

• Don’t start a business when your energy is low (for example, after 60).
  • People now live to 80–100. Don’t wait for inheritance: by the time you get it at 75, you won’t have the energy to use it.
  • At 20–25, you lack money, but good ideas can raise money quickly.

blocks.html:
• Everyone has 24 hours. Sleep 6–8 hours every day, not less than 6 and not more than 8, even on Sunday. Don’t “catch up” sleep on weekends.

  • Rule of 10,000 hours (Malcolm Gladwell, Outliers): about 10,000 hours of focused practice make you an expert.

What an
entrepreneur must know: the 7 business functions

blocks.html: You need vertical expertise (deep skill in your field) and horizontal exposure (some knowledge of every business function):

blocks.html:
Function What you must understand
1. Marketing Reaching customers: B2B (business to business), B2C (business to consumer), digital. High-margin products (e.g. stitching a designer blouse; consulting).
2. Sales Selling your idea; pricing; product mix. Some things are given free to build a platform (like Android).
3. Suppliers For manufacturing: tier 1, 2, 3 suppliers. Don’t depend on just one. Control the cost of goods.
4. Operations Remove non-value-added work. Span of control about 1:7 (one manager, about 7 people). Do it right the first time; rework is waste. Hire the right people.
5. Innovation Business models change every few years: Nokia → BlackBerry → touchscreen phones. Protect ideas with patents (intellectual property). Be fast to market.
6. Support HR, finance, admin, security. Know ROA, ROE, ROCE (returns on assets, equity, capital employed), MIS dashboards, and the RACI matrix (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed).
7. Leadership and management In small and medium businesses, this can’t be delegated. You need clarity, focus and insight.

blocks.text: Foundations

blocks.html:
• Life has three parts: health (most important), wealth, relationships. Use time, energy, resources and money well.
  • Wealth mantra: cash inflows → cash outflows → investment options → return on investment.
  • Inflows: you work for money (human capital, salary); money works for you (assets); gifts and inheritance (don’t count on these).
  • Outflows: hold, spend, donate, invest.
  • Investing: lending or ownership; you control it, or someone else does.
  • Wealth = assets − liabilities.

Money stories

blocks.html:
• Compounding is the “eighth wonder” (quote credited to Einstein).
  • Warren Buffett: $6,000 at 15 → about $85 billion by 88; most of it after 56. Regret: started late.
  • Oseola McCarty: a washerwoman who gave $150,000 to a university.
  • Boris Becker, Michael Jackson, Ranbaxy: earning a lot ≠ managing well.
  • Good liabilities: a small education loan, a startup, a joint home. Bad: personal loan (24% a year), credit card (36%), car loan, gadgets on EMI.

blocks.html: 1. Save before you spend (20%+). 2. Emergency fund (3–6 months). 3. Term insurance (100 × monthly income). 4. Own health insurance. 5. Returns, inflation,
compounding

blocks.html:
• Inflation = rising prices = falling purchasing power. “Too much money chasing too few goods.” It is measured by the CPI.
  • India: about 6–7% overall; education about 10%; health up to 15%.
  • ROI = net profit ÷ cost × 100.
  • CAGR example: ₹1 crore → ₹1.48 crore in 5 years. Simple 9.6% a year, but CAGR 8.16%.
  • Use XIRR for SIPs. ETF = passive (benchmark return); an active fund must beat the benchmark.

Income tax (lecture: FY
2022–23)

blocks.html:
• 5 heads: salaries, house property, capital gains, business or profession, other sources.
  • Old regime: 5% / 20% / 30% above ₹10 lakh, with deductions (80C, 80D, NPS).
  • New regime: 5% steps up to 30% above ₹15 lakh, without deductions.
  • Lecture’s rule: save about ₹2.5 lakh a year → old regime; otherwise → new regime.
  • Today: the new regime is the default, and income up to ₹12 lakh is effectively tax-free under it.
  • Tax planning is ethical; evasion is not.

Employee vs entrepreneur

blocks.html:
• About 15 of 100 startups survive 3 years. High risk, high reward.
  • Time, money, energy: young = time and energy, no money; 26–50 = money and energy, no time; 50+ = energy falls.
  • Sleep 6–8 hours. Remember the 10,000-hour rule and learning → earning → returning.
  • 7 business functions: marketing, sales, suppliers, operations, innovation, support, leadership.
  • Risk only about 20% of your money. Work 5–6 years first. Don’t start at 60.

Asset allocation

blocks.html:
• Personal balance sheet every year: net worth = assets − liabilities. Beat inflation with a positive real return.
  • RBI bonds: safe but taxable. FDs: use laddering, and keep deposits within ₹5 lakh insurance per bank. Corporate deposits: capital risk. Gold: max 10%. Real estate: illiquid.
  • Equity sizes: giant, large, mid, small, micro. Ways in: mutual fund (₹100), PMS (₹50 lakh), AIF (₹1 crore).
  • Four risks: liquidity, credit, volatility, concentration. Make a will (or your assets are intestate).
  • Financial freedom = income from assets is greater than expenses.
